questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a food chain?

options.text: A sequence showing the flow of energy from one organism to another
A chart showing population changes over time
A diagram showing the classification of organisms
A list of all species in an ecosystem

questions.explanation: A food chain is a sequence showing the flow of energy from one organism to another through feeding relationships. It starts with a producer and shows the direction of energy transfer through consumers.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between energy flow and nutrient cycling in ecosystems?

options.text: Both energy and nutrients are recycled equally
Energy flows in one direction and is lost as heat; nutrients are recycled
Energy is recycled but nutrients are not
Nutrients flow in one direction and energy is recycled

questions.explanation: Energy flows in one direction through ecosystems and is lost as heat at each trophic level. Nutrients (carbon, nitrogen) are recycled through biogeochemical cycles, being reused repeatedly by organisms.

questions.stem: In the carbon cycle, which process converts atmospheric CO2 into organic compounds?

options.text: Decomposition
Combustion
Respiration
Photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis converts atmospheric carbon dioxide into organic compounds (glucose). This is the main way carbon enters living systems from the atmosphere, forming the basis of food chains.

questions.stem: What would happen to an ecosystem if all decomposers were removed?

options.text: Dead matter would accumulate and nutrients would not be recycled back into the soil
Plants would grow faster
Nothing would change
Predators would increase in number

questions.explanation: Without decomposers, dead organisms and waste would accumulate, and essential nutrients would not be recycled back into the soil. Plants would eventually run out of minerals, causing the entire food web to collapse.

questions.stem: Which human activity has the greatest impact on increasing atmospheric CO2?

options.text: Burning fossil fuels
Planting trees
Recycling waste
Using renewable energy

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon that was stored underground for millions of years, significantly increasing atmospheric CO2 levels. This is the largest human contribution to enhanced greenhouse effect and climate change.

questions.stem: Why do predator and prey populations show cyclical changes?

options.text: Because they are not related to each other
Because the climate changes in cycles
Because increases in prey lead to increases in predators, which then reduce prey numbers
Because both populations always increase together

questions.explanation: Predator-prey populations cycle because more prey means more food for predators, so predator numbers increase. More predators then eat more prey, causing prey numbers to fall, which then causes predator numbers to fall, and the cycle repeats.

questions.stem: What is the best description of sustainable development?

options.text: Never using any natural resources
Using resources in a way that meets current needs without compromising future generations
Using resources as quickly as possible for economic growth
Only using renewable energy sources

questions.explanation: Sustainable development means using resources at a rate that meets present needs while ensuring future generations can also meet their needs. It balances economic development, social wellbeing, and environmental protection.
